text:
emma: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — I sketched a 'staging matrix' for precision lanes to help ops/runtime coordinate rollouts. want quick eyes. :eyes:

raj: drop it here pls, curious how you map customer endpoints to lanes.

emma: pasted below. idea: each endpoint gets a 'precision lane' (safe, balanced, aggressive). lanes map to profile sets: fp16/int8/fp8/4bit combos. runtime uses request metadata + SLOs to pick lane.

linda: hmm. how do we prevent silent quality regressions when we move endpoints to aggressive?

emma: three levers: 1) per-endpoint eval suite (golden prompts) run on every change, 2) online drift telemetry + degradation score, 3) automatic graceful fallback to prev stable lane on quality loss.

jorge: can you show the matrix? also how does this interact with A/B or canary?

emma: matrix (rough):
```
endpoint_type -> allowed_lanes -> default_lane -> canary_window
search_api -> [safe, balanced] -> balanced -> 2% traffic 24h
chat_completions -> [balanced, aggressive] -> balanced -> 5% 48h
billing_reports -> [safe] -> safe -> none
embedding_batch -> [aggressive] -> aggressive -> 10% offpeak
```

emma: runtime picks lane by evaluating: endpoint metadata, user SLA tier, request CPU/GPU budget header, and recent quality signal. canary windows are enforced by router to limit traffic.

raj: sounds reasonable. where does quantization profile metadata live? model artifact or serving config?

emma: plan is model artifact carries canonical profiles (recommended runtime mapping) + a lightweight serving config per endpoint to override. keeps model portability but lets ops tune per-customer.

linda: edge case: what if a new fp8 kernel lands that has perf win but different numeric stability? we need a preflight process.

emma: agreed — preflight steps: unit microbench on canary infra, golden-prompt regressions, 24h canary with synthetic traffic, and an automated rollback hook if degscore > threshold. i'll draft playbook.

jorge: API surface question: should callers be able to hint precision? i worry about apps gaming it and pushing to aggressive to cut cost.

linda: yes — allow hints but honor tenant-level quotas and a hard server-side override. also require a 'risky-precision' feature flag per customer.

emma: sketch of serving-config snippet (for the console / terraform):
```
precision_config: {
  default_lane: "balanced",
  allowed_lanes: ["safe","balanced","aggressive"],
  eval_suite: "gs://redwood-eval/search_gold_v2",
  canary: { pct: 5, duration_hours: 48 }
}
```

raj: telemetry: we need token-level alignments to surface which prompts degrade. heavy but useful. can we do sampled telemetry + shadow evals?

emma: yes — sampling + targeted shadowing on golden prompts. degscore is computed from ngram overlap + embedding-sim + task-specific metrics. we store fingerprints per-run.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary policy applied for endpoint=chat_completions, pct=5, duration=48h.

linda: compatibility question: if endpoint moves from balanced->aggressive, do we trigger a model-variant rollout? or same model with different runtime quant profile?

emma: prefer runtime-only quant switch (no model recompile) for speed. but if profile requires recompiled kernels we treat as model-variant and follow model rollout slate.

jorge: sounds good. one more: metrics for SRE — want latency P95, degscore, and cost-per-1k-tokens by lane. add to dashboard.

emma: noted. i'll add to console dashboard board: lane breakdown: p50/p95, degscore, cost. Also add an alert: degscore delta > 0.12 triggers pager.

raj: ok let's get this into an RFC follow-up doc. thanks. :thumbsup:

emma: i'll draft RFC addendum and a short ops-runbook. ping me if you want to take sections.

linda: i'll own the eval-suite integration.

jorge: i'll take the router/canary enforcement piece.

emma: thanks all. closing thread for now. if anything urgent, re-open. :v:
